name: libcxxabi

patches.reason: This project's own crt1.o never defines __dso_handle (Bionic's real crtbegin/crtend split is not imported), and libc++abi's static-init-guard code needs a real symbol of that exact name to reference. A tiny CRT-owned shim source, wired into libcxxabi's own build via this one-line CMakeLists.txt insertion rather than patched into the freestanding CRT startup objects themselves.

patches.find:
if (MINGW)
  # MINGW_LIBRARIES is defined in config-ix.cmake
  list(APPEND LIBCXXABI_LIBRARIES ${MINGW_LIBRARIES})
endif()
patches.replace:
# CRT: MINGW_LIBRARIES (mingw32/moldname/mingwex/msvcrt/advapi32/...) is
# a real mingw-w64 distribution's own CRT stub import libraries -- this
# project's --target=*-w64-mingw32 is used for ABI/calling-convention
# compatibility only, never a real mingw-w64 install, so none of these
# exist in the sysroot at all (confirmed for real: "lld: error: unable
# to find library -lmingw32" and 15 siblings). tools/crt-c++ already
# supplies the complete real link line (this project's own kernel32.lib/
# synchronization.lib, its own libc, no mingw-w64 runtime at all), so
# this block is a deliberate no-op here rather than a real port.
if (FALSE)
endif()
patches.reason: CMake's built-in MINGW variable is true for any *-w64-mingw32 target regardless of whether a real mingw-w64 CRT distribution actually backs it -- this project's own kernel32.lib/synchronization.lib and Bionic-shaped libc already satisfy everything a real Windows program needs, added by tools/crt-c++ itself; MINGW_LIBRARIES names real mingw-w64 runtime stub libraries this sysroot has never had and will never provide.

patches.replace:
add_definitions(-D_LIBCXXABI_BUILDING_LIBRARY)
# CRT: _LIBCXXABI_BUILDING_LIBRARY (above) only controls libcxxabi's own
# headers -- it does NOT flip libcxx/include/__config's separate
# _LIBCPP_BUILDING_LIBRARY switch, which decides whether
# _LIBCPP_EXCEPTION_ABI (used by <stdexcept>/<typeinfo>'s class
# declarations) expands to dllexport or dllimport on Windows. Three of
# libcxxabi's own src/*.cpp files (fallback_malloc.cpp,
# stdlib_exception.cpp, stdlib_new_delete.cpp) already self-#define
# _LIBCPP_BUILDING_LIBRARY for exactly this reason; stdlib_stdexcept.cpp
# and stdlib_typeinfo.cpp do not, so without this they define
# std::runtime_error/bad_cast/bad_typeid's vtables against a dllimport
# declaration -- silently accepted with a "redeclared without 'dllimport'
# attribute" warning, but the vtable itself never gets dllexport'd, so
# cxxabi_shared/libc++abi.dll's own link fails with "undefined symbol:
# vtable for std::runtime_error" and two siblings. Real upstream LLVM
# never hits this because its blessed build configures libcxx and
# libcxxabi together in one CMake project graph sharing one such define;
# this project's three-separate-recipe build does not have that, so it
# needs to set this explicitly.
add_definitions(-D_LIBCPP_BUILDING_LIBRARY)
patches.reason: Confirmed for real: cxxabi_shared/libc++abi.dll's link failed with 'ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: __declspec(dllimport) vtable for std::runtime_error' and two siblings (std::bad_cast, std::bad_typeid) -- traced to stdlib_stdexcept.cpp/stdlib_typeinfo.cpp defining these vtables under a dllimport declaration (from libcxx's own <stdexcept>/<typeinfo> headers) because _LIBCPP_BUILDING_LIBRARY was never defined for libcxxabi's own build, only its unrelated _LIBCXXABI_BUILDING_LIBRARY sibling macro.

notes: Deliberately no LIBCXXABI_USE_LLVM_UNWINDER/LIBCXXABI_LIBUNWIND_INCLUDES here, on any host: that CMake option only changes libcxxabi's own compile-time #ifdef selection (real libunwind.h API vs. the generic, portable Itanium _Unwind_* ABI surface) -- it does not, by itself, make the CMake-standalone-build cxxabi_shared/cxxabi_static targets actually link against a real libunwind (that automatic wiring only fires inside a combined, single-configure LLVM "runtimes" build where libunwind was add_subdirectory()'d into the *same* CMake project graph, which AOSP's split-repo layout -- libcxx/libcxxabi/libunwind are three separate git repos -- makes impractical here anyway; confirmed by reading libcxxabi's own src/CMakeLists.txt, which checks `TARGET unwind_shared`/`HAVE_LIBUNWIND`, neither ever satisfiable from a separate `cmake -S -B` invocation). The plain default (this option OFF) Itanium ABI surface libcxxabi already compiles against is exactly what a real libunwind exports too.

The 'dependencies': ['libunwind'] link and the windows CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS override above exist for a real, empirically-found reason, correcting an earlier (wrong) assumption in this file that a link-time reference in tools/crt-c++ alone would be enough: the STATIC cxxabi_static/libc++abi.a build genuinely does not need libunwind's symbols resolved at its own link step (ar does not check for undefined references, confirmed -- it linked clean with zero libunwind anywhere in scope) but the SHARED cxxabi_shared/libc++abi.dll build does, unconditionally -- unlike an ELF .so, a Windows DLL must resolve every referenced symbol (_Unwind_Resume, _Unwind_RaiseException, vtable for std::logic_error/std::runtime_error/std::bad_cast/std::bad_typeid, ...) at its own link time, confirmed for real via 'ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: _Unwind_Resume' and nine siblings the first time LIBCXXABI_ENABLE_SHARED=ON actually got exercised. This links against libunwind's own shared import library (not the static archive) so the actual unwinder code lives in exactly one place (unwind.dll) with libc++abi.dll importing it, avoiding a duplicate-symbol risk against the separate libunwind.a tools/crt-c++'s own *static*-linkage cxx_runtime_libs still adds directly at the final consumer.

macos needs nothing special here either: LIBCXXABI_USE_LLVM_UNWINDER simply stays at its upstream default (OFF), matching Darwin's own already-verified-working libSystem unwinder -- and macos never enables the libunwind dependency at all (see ../libunwind/recipe.json's own target_os), so this recipe's 'dependencies' entry is silently skipped there, matching every other disabled-dependency case tools/crt-libcxx-build.py's resolve_build_order() already handles.

Linux was reached 2026-08-21 (see HISTORY.md's dated entry): unlike Windows, cxxabi_shared/libc++abi.so's own standalone CMake build linked clean with zero libunwind anywhere in scope, needing no target_overrides.linux equivalent of the Windows CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS override above -- confirms the ELF-tolerates-undefined-shlib-symbols reasoning in the note above this one applies the same way to libunwind as it already did to libc.a's own symbols (getauxval() et al, see tools/crt-cc's own -Wl,--start-group fix). The target_overrides.linux entry actually needed instead was unrelated: -DLIBCXXABI_HAS_CXA_THREAD_ATEXIT_IMPL=OFF, because this project's own CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_TARGET_TYPE=STATIC_LIBRARY setting (crt-libcxx-build.py) makes every check_library_exists/check_function_exists probe in config-ix.cmake report a false 'found' (try_compile only ever compiles-and-archives, never actually links, so an undefined symbol can never surface) -- confirmed by reproducing the identical check_library_exists probe by hand through tools/crt-cc, which genuinely fails to link __cxa_thread_atexit_impl against this project's real libc. Forcing the flag off supplies the correct answer the probe cannot reach, and lets libcxxabi fall back to its own portable, already-implemented __cxa_atexit()-and-TLS-key-based cxa_thread_atexit.cpp path instead of expecting a Bionic API-23+ extension this project's libc does not (yet) implement.
